why: Split verdict. (A) schema.py+transitions.py+durable.py+mappers.py (~612 ln): the sqlite ledger/allow-list core. Real libraries exist but don't fit: FSM libs skip persistence/concurrency; SQLAlchemy+Alembic is overkill for 12 flat JSON-blob tables; Temporal/Prefect/Dagster/Celery/APScheduler solve distributed scheduling, not a same-process 7-state ledger -> keep-ours, EXCEPT durable.py (zero production callers) -> delete-ours. (B) remaining ~6086 ln of gastown/depth-harness domain logic (rubric, guardrails, provenance, TUI, roster HR) has no named competitor -> keep-ours by default.

alternatives.name: transitions (pytransitions)
alternatives.covers: Declarative State/Transition/Machine classes with callbacks, conditions, nested states for modeling a graph like PASS_LIFECYCLE.
alternatives.gap: No persistence, no concurrency control; the sqlite BEGIN IMMEDIATE guarded read-check-insert (the actual hard part) stays hand-written regardless of this library.
alternatives.cost: New dependency; learn a Machine API for a graph our flat dict already expresses in ~10 lines.

alternatives.name: python-statemachine
alternatives.covers: Class+decorator based FSM: states, transitions, guards, on_enter/on_exit hooks.
alternatives.gap: Same as pytransitions: pure in-memory model, no sqlite/ledger/concurrency; would sit on top of our existing I/O layer, not replace it.
alternatives.cost: New dependency + decorator API to learn for a 7-state linear graph.

alternatives.name: sqlite-utils
alternatives.covers: Programmatic table creation/upsert/FTS helpers over sqlite3; CLI + library from the Datasette ecosystem.
alternatives.gap: No concurrency-safe guarded-transition logic; would shrink schema.py's DDL string by roughly 30-60 lines, not the transition-guard logic in transitions.py.
alternatives.cost: One new dependency; DDL rewritten as .create() calls.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained; v4.0 shipped 2026-07-07 (confirmed via WebSearch).

alternatives.name: SQLAlchemy + Alembic
alternatives.covers: ORM models plus a real versioned migration system (upgrade/downgrade scripts, autogenerate diffs).
alternatives.gap: Would require rewriting dozens of hand-written parameterized queries across cli.py/mappers.py/retrieval.py/text_index.py/eval_cmds.py into ORM models for 12 flat JSON-blob tables with no real joins.
alternatives.cost: Large rewrite (see migration_loc); an ORM engine/session layer to maintain going forward.
alternatives.maturity: Extremely mature, industry standard, actively maintained.

alternatives.name: Temporal (self-hosted OSS)
alternatives.covers: Durable, replay-safe distributed workflow execution across workers; ships a genuinely free single-binary local dev server (temporal server start-dev, sqlite-backed), confirmed via WebSearch.
alternatives.gap: Solves distributed/long-running worker orchestration; this code guards a same-process 7-state ledger with no workers, no remote activities, no multi-day timers to justify replay-determinism workflows.
alternatives.cost: A running server+worker process pair, workflow/activity code restructuring, gRPC.

alternatives.name: Prefect / Dagster / Celery / APScheduler
alternatives.covers: Task scheduling (APScheduler), distributed task queues (Celery, needs a broker), asset/DAG orchestration (Dagster), flow orchestration (Prefect).
alternatives.gap: None model an allow-list state-transition ledger; adopting any means bolting sqlite persistence back on top of a scheduler solving a different problem.
alternatives.cost: Celery needs Redis/RabbitMQ; Prefect/Dagster need a server process; APScheduler doesn't fit the problem at all.
alternatives.maturity: All mature, actively maintained OSS projects.

evidence: Read schema.py/transitions.py/durable.py in full (258+158+81 ln); skimmed docstrings of all 41 top-level .py files. grep for advance_pass|current_pass_state|revert_pass|PASS_LIFECYCLE in src/ matches only those 2 files. grep for DurableBackend|InMemoryBackend in src/ matches only durable.py (6 occ). cli.py has its own separate ILLEGAL_TRANSITIONS deny-list (ln52-57, 672-715) on the same table.
recheck: grep -rn "advance_pass|current_pass_state|revert_pass|PASS_LIFECYCLE|DurableBackend|InMemoryBackend" intent-control-plane/src -- if any file besides transitions.py/durable.py now matches, the delete-ours call on durable.py is stale.
migration_loc: Keep subsystem A/B as-is (0 lines). Delete durable.py: -81 src lines, -82 test lines (test_durable.py), ~-8 lines trimmed from transitions.py's cross-referencing docstring.
what_ours_does: ~612 ln (schema/transitions/durable/mappers): sqlite DDL+connection mgmt+a guarded 7-state allow-list pass-lifecycle machine with a swappable in-memory backend. ~6086 ln remaining (cli, tower, retrieval, project_map, standards, guardrails, rubric, company, archive, provenance): bespoke gastown/depth-harness logic - calibration, reward-hacking screens, persona grading, scorecards, TUI.
strongest_counterargument: sqlite-utils (v4.0 shipped 2026-07-07, confirmed) or Alembic would give a tested migration path that is genuinely missing today: SCHEMA_VERSION=3 is stamped with no ALTER-based upgrade, only additive CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. If this ledger ever needs a non-additive schema change, today's code has no story for it and one would have to be written ad hoc anyway.
